outcomes: Train a one-hidden-layer ReLU classifier with real gradients
Explain initialization and diagnose inactive units
Save and validate complete resumable optimizer checkpoints

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.definition: An optimizer method that updates a running velocity from current and past gradients.
momentum.explanation: In this chapter, velocity equals beta times the previous velocity plus the current gradient, and parameters subtract learning rate times velocity. The memory can smooth noisy directions and carry movement through small gradients. Different libraries use related but differently scaled conventions, so checkpoint state and documentation must match the implementation. Momentum adds one state value per parameter and that state is required for an exact training resume.

adam.name: Adam
adam.definition: An optimizer using bias-corrected moving averages of gradients and squared gradients.
adam.explanation: Adam tracks a first moment resembling momentum and a second raw moment that scales updates by recent gradient magnitude. Because both buffers start at zero, the algorithm corrects their initial bias using the step count. Its epsilon prevents division by zero. An Adam checkpoint needs parameters, both moment arrays, step, learning rate, beta coefficients, and epsilon. Adam often trains conveniently, but it does not guarantee generalization or eliminate hyperparameter selection.

checkpoint.name: Checkpoint
checkpoint.definition: A validated snapshot of model and training state saved for later use.
checkpoint.explanation: Inference may need only architecture and parameter values. Exact training resume additionally needs optimizer buffers, step counters, and hyperparameters, and may need scheduler or random-state data in larger systems. A safe loader verifies version, dimensions, lengths, finite numbers, and optimizer constraints before allocating or using values. Writing through a temporary file reduces partial-target risk. A checkpoint is executable data at a trust boundary, so malformed input must fail clearly.

sources.title: Some Methods of Speeding Up the Convergence of Iteration Methods

checks: Both momentum and Adam reduce fixture loss
A hidden parameter gradient matches central differences away from a ReLU kink
Save/restore preserves the exact next Adam update
Corrupt or unsafe checkpoint dimensions and values are rejected
Zero-epoch evaluation requires an existing checkpoint and preserves its bytes
Nonfinite loss, gradients, and optimizer moments are rejected
limitations: The 16-unit MLP is an educational baseline
The binary checkpoint format is course-specific and little-endian
The safe-write path does not sync the parent directory
